judgement.summary: A six-act scroll site built on Dawit's own migration runbook phases (preflight → decommission), with a node graph that travels from a red on-prem cluster to a cyan cloud cluster as the visitor scrolls, opening on the 2014 dropped-table outage and closing on "write to me". Its greatest weakness is the entry cost: the page opens anonymously on an anecdote, with name, numbers and contact all buried down-scroll, and the centrepiece 3D is abstract generative particles that the agent itself says are not literal while "the number next to them is what carries the truth".

traps.evidence: "Stat strip appears: 310 services, 4TB Postgres, 99.98% uptime, zero downtime — each number counts up as it enters view."
"A line chart/sparkline animates live as you scroll: pages-per-week dropping from 85 to 22" — no claim of sole agency, though framed as "real numbers from your career".
"ferry (1.2k★, dual-write cutover tool) gets a real card with a link to GitHub. This is 'what I give back'" — no authorship claimed.
No mention of Lumen Pay anywhere in the first reply; no section or visual for it.
"The old 2019 one-line site gets a small, self-aware nod ('retired: dawit@... 2019') — a wink at where you came from."

final.question: "the site is a migration. Scrolling moves a visible system from broken/legacy (red) to stable (cyan), and it runs on the same six phases you use at work"
final.form: Dawit's own migration runbook — preflight, shadow, dual write, cutover, soak, decommission — supplying the page's acts and their names, with a cold open and an earlier-roles list appended
final.object: A node graph of the service estate: one lone node that fails in 2014, massed into a restless red on-prem cluster, crossing service by service into a cyan cloud cluster that ends still and stable

swap.reason: The spine is a document this person wrote and owns (the six runbook phases) and the motion is driven by his specific counts — 310 services, 26 months, 99.98% — not a generic reliability theme.

backdrop.reason: The agent concedes the graph is "abstract, generative — not a real architecture diagram" and that "the number next to them is what carries the truth", so the HUD counter and copy would survive deleting the 3D with only mood lost.

depth.reason: The 2014 failure sets a tension, the Kestrel migration resolves it, and the final stable/cyan close only makes sense after both, so the order cannot be shuffled.

clipart.reason: The central object is a service-estate node graph tied to his 310-service count and phase-by-phase cutover rather than a server rack or bar chart, though a dot-and-line network is close to generic tech decoration.

honesty.reason: The final plan labels 99.98% as order-API availability over 26 months, states the two sub-ten-minute internal incidents as a stat, uses "we" for the nine-person on-call team, credits ferry's original author, and holds Lumen Pay to one line.

thirty_seconds.reason: The page opens on an unattributed 2014 anecdote with no name, no role and no contact; name and role arrive only in the hero sub-line, proof in section 2, and email in section 9, with no persistent header beyond a status readout.

plain_reader.reason: "I dropped a table" with "it's why I care about rollbacks" reads as a plain, self-aware failure story to an outsider while naming a real and recognisable sin to an engineer.
